Using CSS, you can add elements to a page that do not exist in the page layout. This is done using the <code>:before</code> and <code>:after</code> pseudo-elements, but the <code>content</code> property plays an equally important role in this.<!--more-->

It defines the contents of pseudo-elements. And even more, pseudo-elements will not be displayed if they do not have the <code>content</code> property set. The following line is enough:

```css
content: "";
```

The specification is here: <a href="http://www.w3.org/TR/css3-content/">w3.org/TR/css3-content/</a>

The snowmen in the example are added using <code>content</code> for pseudo-elements, the snowmen themselves are Unicode characters:

```css
DIV:before {
  content: "\2603";
}
```

<iframe class="live-snippet" style="height: 200px" src="../assets/demo/content/demo_1.html?output"></iframe>

**Possible property values:**

<code>normal</code>, <code>none</code> - the contents of the pseudo-element are not displayed. Useful if you need to hide a previously specified pseudo-element.

<code><string></code> - text content. You can insert plain text and Unicode characters, as in the example above. For practical purposes, different arrow options are very useful. Unicode characters can be found, for example, <a href="https://yoksel.github.io/unicode-table/">here</a> or <a href="http://unicode-table.com/ru/">here</a>.

```css
DIV:before  {
  content: "Hello";
}
```

<iframe class="live-snippet" style="height: 200px" src="../assets/demo/content/demo_2.html?output"></iframe>

<iframe class="live-snippet" style="height: 200px" src="../assets/demo/content/demo_3.html?output"></iframe>

<code><uri></code> - addresses of pictures.


```css
DIV:before  {
  content: url(//img-fotki.yandex.ru/get/5413/5091629.67/0_5ba12_81d03a82_XS.png);
}
```

<iframe class="live-snippet" style="height: 250px" src="../assets/demo/content/demo_4.html?output"></iframe>

Practical application - icons before links to profiles on social networks, an icon to indicate an external link, list bulletins.

<iframe class="live-snippet" style="height: 270px" src="../assets/demo/content/demo_5.html?output"></iframe>

However, here there is a problem of unnecessary requests to the server.

Solutions options:

* sprite, icons from which are inserted in the background into the link itself or into a pseudo-element. The second is preferable, because then the pseudo-element will limit the visibility area of the sprite, so the icons in the sprite can be arranged not only vertically, but also in rows.<br>
The number of requests to the server is reduced to one, but the image is cached by the user;
* encode individual images in base-64 and insert via <code>content: url()</code>;
* encode the entire sprite in base-64 and use it as the background for the pseudo-element.

In the last two options there will be no requests to the server at all, but the images are not cached and, in addition, the encoded image may weigh more than the original one. It makes sense to use this method only for small images.

You can encode a picture in base64 using online services. The resulting code is inserted into <code>url()</code> with information about the format of the content, for example <code>data:image/png;base64</code>.

This is what the code for the Instagram icon will look like:

```css
[href*="instagram.com"]:before {
    content: url(data:image/png;base64,)
}
```

The code is long and ends somewhere over the horizon. In addition, it is not clear from the code what kind of picture is in it, and if it is necessary to edit it, the picture will have to be encoded and inserted again each time, although in the case of a regular image it will simply need to be re-uploaded. At the same time, there is a plugin for grant that automatically encodes pictures and replaces the addresses of pictures in the code with base64.

You can insert SVG in the same way.

```css
DIV:before{
	content: url('data:image/svg+xml;utf8,&lt;svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="32" height="32">&lt;path d="M19.414 27.414l10-10c0.781-0.781 0.781-2.047 0-2.828l-10-10c-0.781-0.781-2.047-0.781-2.828 0-0.781 0.781-0.781 2.047 0 2.828l6.586 6.586h-19.172c-1.105 0-2 0.895-2 2s0.895 2 2 2h19.172l-6.586 6.586c-0.39 0.39-0.586 0.902-0.586 1.414s0.195 1.024 0.586 1.414c0.781 0.781 2.047 0.781 2.828 0z" fill="#FFF" />&lt;/svg>');
	}
```

This is very convenient, but does not yet work in all browsers. For example, Chrome will understand and display this, but Firefox will not.

<strong>Upd:</strong> SVG in CSS will work in all browsers if you code it as an address bar. This can be done using <a href="https://yoksel.github.io/url-encoder/ru/">URL Encoder</a>.

<code><counter></code> - counter. Using this value, you can number not only lists, but also any elements on the page. For example, sections of an article.

```css
BODY {
  counter-reset: h2-counter;
  counter-reset: p-counter;
}

DIV {
  counter-increment: h2-counter;
}

H2:before {
  content: counter(h2-counter) ". ";
}

P:before {
  content: counter(p-counter) ". ";
  counter-increment: p-counter;
}
```

<code>counter-reset</code> specifies the name of the counter.

<code>counter-increment</code> increases the value of the given counter.

<code>content: counter(counter name)</code> outputs the counter value as the content of a pseudo-element.

<iframe class="live-snippet" style="height: 420px" src="../assets/demo/content/demo_6.html?output"></iframe>

<code>attr(<identifier>) </code> - This value displays the contents of the specified attribute. Convenient to use for displaying <code>href</code> attributes in print versions and for various interesting effects.

```css
A:before  {
  content: attr(title);
}
```

<iframe class="live-snippet" style="height: 200px" src="../assets/demo/content/demo_7.html?output"></iframe>

Many effects can be found here: <a href="http://tympanus.net/Development/CreativeLinkEffects/">tympanus.net/Development/CreativeLinkEffects/</a>

<code>open-quote</code>, <code>close-quote</code> - values ​​for displaying opening and closing quotes. The characters that will be used are determined by the <code>quotes</code> property. If not set, default values ​​will be used, which vary by browser.

```css
BLOCKQUOTE {
	quotes: '"' '"' "'" "'";
}
BLOCKQUOTE:before {
  content: open-quote;
  }
BLOCKQUOTE:after  {
  content: close-quote;
  }
```

<iframe class="live-snippet" style="height: 200px" src="../assets/demo/content/demo_8.html?output"></iframe>

<code>no-open-quote</code>, <code>no-close-quote</code> - the value disables the display of quotes, but the level of their nesting continues to be taken into account.

There is a lot more interesting stuff in the <a href="http://www.w3.org/TR/css3-content/">specification</a> like a pseudo-element representing a wrapper for an entire element or multiple pseudo-elements, but this is not implemented anywhere at the moment.
